title: Dismiss the blocker
brief:
A cookie-consent panel is covering the shop. This test tries to click straight past it.

**Run it first.** It takes a moment - Playwright retries for the full 30 seconds before giving up - and the call log tells you precisely what stopped it.

Then fix it by dismissing the panel first. The real site does the same thing, and so does `pages/base_page.py`:

```python
consent_button = self.page.get_by_role("button", name="Consent")
if consent_button.count() > 0 and consent_button.first.is_visible():
    consent_button.first.click()
```

Here the panel is always there, so you can just click it - no `if` needed.
starter:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_products_page_opens_past_the_consent_panel(page: Page):
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/")

    page.get_by_role("link", name="Products").click()

    expect(page.get_by_role("heading", name="All Products")).to_be_visible()
solution:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_products_page_opens_past_the_consent_panel(page: Page):
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/")

    # Nothing on the page is clickable until this is out of the way.
    page.get_by_role("button", name="Consent").click()

    page.get_by_role("link", name="Products").click()

    expect(page.get_by_role("heading", name="All Products")).to_be_visible()

checks.label: The consent panel has been dismissed
checks.feedback: The panel is still up at the end of your test. Click the Consent button before anything else - while it is open, every click underneath it is intercepted.

checks.label: The Products link click got through

checks.name: to_be_visible
checks.label: You still assert the heading rendered

hints.label: Nudge
hints.text: Read the call log: "<div class="consent-popup"> intercepts pointer events". Playwright found your link. Something was on top of it.

hints.label: Strategy
hints.text: Add one line before the Products click: click the button whose accessible name is Consent. Its role is button, not link.

hints.label: Solution
hints.text: page.get_by_role("button", name="Consent").click() as the first action after goto.

reveal:
This is the failure that makes people add `time.sleep(5)` and move on - and the sleep never helps, because time was never the problem.

Read the call log instead. `intercepts pointer events` names the element that was in the way, and the fix is always the same: deal with the thing in the way.

It is also why the kit's `BasePage.open()` dismisses consent as part of *opening a page* rather than leaving it to every test.
